In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''Virasoro conjecture''' states that a certain [[generating function]] encoding [[Gromov–Witten invariant]]s of a [[singular point of an algebraic variety|smooth]] [[projective variety]] is fixed by an action of half of the [[Virasoro algebra]]. The Virasoro conjecture is named after [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] [[Miguel Ángel Virasoro (physicist)|Miguel Ángel Virasoro]]. {{harvs|txt | last3=Xiong | first3=Chuan-Sheng | last2=Hori | first2=Kentaro | last1=Eguchi | first1=Tohru | title=Quantum cohomology and Virasoro algebra | url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/S0370-2693(97)00401-2 | doi=10.1016/S0370-2693(97)00401-2 |mr=1454328 | year=1997 | journal=Physics Letters B | issn=0370-2693 | volume=402 | issue=1 | pages=71–80}}
proposed the Virasoro conjecture as a generalization of [[Witten's conjecture]]. {{harvs|txt|last=Getzler|first=Ezra|authorlink=Ezra Getzler|year=1999}} gave a survey of the Virasoro conjecture.

The proof of the genus 0 Virasoro conjecture for all smooth projective varieties (or more generally, compact symplectic manifolds) was first given by [[Xiaobo Liu (mathematician)|Xiaobo Liu]] and [[Tian Gang|Gang Tian]] (1998).<ref>{{Citation |last1=Liu |first1=Xiaobo |title=Virasoro Constraints For Quantum Cohomology |date=1998-10-20 |last2=Tian |first2=Gang|arxiv=math/9806028 |bibcode=1998math......6028L }}</ref>
